page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with shared CPU allocation and 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks present a mixed profile. The instance achieves a top-tier rating in Geekbench single-core testing and a strong rating in Geekbench text processing. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 10%. Memory read bandwidth is weak, though large-block write bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression perform at average levels. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput are generally weak to poor, reflecting the shared CPU allocation.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU throughput. The shared CPU model introduces potential performance variability, making it less suitable for intensive database operations or high-throughput web serving. It is best suited for lightweight memory-optimized tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, or development environments requiring a larger memory footprint without heavy compute demands.
